title: Six-Point Programme Announced
subtitle: A constitutional roadmap for autonomy in East Pakistan.
summary: In 1966, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman publicly advanced the Six-Point Programme as a constitutional framework for provincial autonomy in Pakistan. The programme reorganized East Pakistan's political demands around representation, fiscal control, and federal restructuring, quickly becoming a defining platform of Bengali nationalist politics.
heroTagline: The Six Points reframed autonomy as a clear constitutional demand.
whyItMatters: The Six-Point Programme transformed scattered grievances into a coherent political agenda, laying essential groundwork for the mass upsurge of 1969 and the independence struggle that followed.
